about: Measured sizes and geometric albedos of the large distant bodies, which JPL's small-body database gives no diameter for. Each value is quoted from its paper (abstract or results), read on 26 Nov 2026 by the RW7 thread; no value is from memory. The catalogue build uses a row only where JPL has no measured diameter, and checks its name against JPL's row. A diameter from a radius or semi-axes is said so in the note.

Ortiz, J. L. et al. 2017, Nature 550, 219: The size, shape, density and ring of the dwarf planet Haumea from a stellar occultation
Brown, M. E. 2013, ApJ 767, L7: On the size, shape, and density of dwarf planet Makemake
Pál, A. et al. 2016, AJ 151, 117: Large size and slow rotation of the trans-Neptunian object (225088) 2007 OR10 discovered from Herschel and K2 observations
Margoti, G. et al. 2026, arXiv:2607.06450: Size, shape, density, and atmospheric limit of (50000) Quaoar revealed from 14 years of stellar occultation
Pál, A. et al. 2012, A&A 541, L6: "TNOs are Cool": A survey of the trans-Neptunian region. VII. Size and surface characteristics of (90377) Sedna and 2010 EK139
Fornasier, S. et al. 2013, A&A 555, A15: "TNOs are Cool": A survey of the trans-Neptunian region. VIII. Combined Herschel PACS and SPIRE observations of nine bright targets at 70-500 um

small_bodies.name: Eris
small_bodies.note: twice the occultation radius 1,163 +/- 6 km; pV 0.96 +0.09/-0.04

small_bodies.name: Haumea
small_bodies.note: volume-equivalent diameter 1,595 +/- 11 km of the triaxial body (semi-axes 1,161, 852, 513 km); pV 0.51 +/- 0.02

small_bodies.name: Quaoar
small_bodies.note: volume-equivalent diameter 1,094.4 +/- 4.6 km from occultations; pV 0.125 +/- 0.038 (a preprint)

small_bodies.name: Orcus
small_bodies.note: radiometric, all data, 958.4 +/- 22.9 km; pV 0.231 +0.018/-0.011 (arXiv v2 table 4)
